display_name: Cynosure Site D (Militech lab beneath the Kress Street hideout)
why: Cynosure Site D is the disused Militech lab the Rindo Hotel's squat lift and subway tunnel lead down to: a metro platform, a mine- and turret-guarded security gauntlet of back offices, and a control room whose monitors and computers still hold Evan McRay's decade-old logs. Nothing lives there - vanilla offers only one community, a video-recording actor inside the quest prefab, and Bree and Dante only appear here for the mq305 break-in and standoff. This proposal restores no people and loads no quest sections; it switches the lab's baked dark state to vanilla's own lit, powered look (entrance lights and leveldesign temp lights) and hides the quest keycard, then records how the way in works.

open_questions: Walk the venue in from the Rindo Hotel: take the squat lift down to the subway level, follow the tunnel to the lab entrance, and report where the route stops and whether the lift's subway floor is callable at all.
Check that #mq305_lab_entrance opens from the tunnel side without the quest, and record what opens it (runtime door policy, quickhack, terminal, or nothing).

Confirm the lab is lit as intended: entrance lights on and leveldesign temp_lights on, with no doubled or z-fighting light meshes at the entrance; if it still reads dark, try the capitalised V_Entrance_On/V_Entrance_Off pair.
Confirm the control room has no quest keycard and no video-recording set or Johnny triggers - the room should look like an abandoned office with monitors and computers only.
Stand in the security gauntlet with the baked state and report whether the cameras, turrets and laser mines are live; that is the difference between a hazard site and a walk-through ruin.

Check the doors against the wiki: which door refuses Bree's Militech card, whether #mq305_backoffice_door_coolant is the alternative route, and whether the Body/Tech 10 door to the defence computer still works.

variant_toggles.why: The streaming block bakes the entrance unlit (var_v_entrance_on enabledByDefault=0, var_v_entrance_off=1). Vanilla's own in-use look is both variants shown: mq305_03_bunker_exploration_setup and the mq305 root graph set var_v_entrance_on=1 and var_v_entrance_off=1 together before the player reaches the lab. Copying that pair lights the entrance for normal play without inventing a state.

temp_lights is baked off (enabledByDefault=0) and vanilla switches it on in its chapter-setup graphs before the lab is entered, i.e. it is the temporary work-light rig that makes the derelict interior readable. Turning it on gives the venue vanilla's own lit look instead of a pitch-black ruin.

Vanilla hides the control room keycard variant before the player explores the lab (mq305 root graph, exploration setup branch), so the keycard is quest dressing the story places and removes. Hiding it keeps the clean slate free of quest props in the control room.

deferred_prefab_owner: world streaming (the chosen people need no quest prefab)

proximity_wait.why: The lab's double entrance door (#loc_mq305_wanted_lab_gameplay/double_door_prefabU6LT2UA/#mq305_lab_entrance), the first device a visitor meets coming off the subway tunnel and the one vanilla itself powers, enables and forces open in the exploration setup. A real DoorControllerPS with a resolved path in the always-streamed gameplay section, never a workspot (rule 8).
